newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU to allow import of extra 13,000 Japanese cars.
newsitem.headline: EU to allow import of extra 13,000 Japanese cars.

text.p: The European Commission said on Friday it would allow Japan to export an extra 13,000 vehicles to the European Union this year following better-than-expected sales figures for 1996.
A European Commission spokesman told a news conference that following a regular meeting to monitor vehicle trade between the EU and Japan, Tokyo's exports would be increased to 1,079,000 units.
The previous figure of 1,066,000 units was based on expected 1996 EU vehicle sales of 13,289,000, a spokesman said.
"This year the market is better than expected," he said. "We are talking about 13,545,000 units for Europe, so about 260,000 units more than agreed back in March."
Japan and the EU have an informal agreement to monitor vehicle trade until the end of the century with direct Japanese exports being based on a percentage of actual sales in the 15-member bloc.

The agreement -- started in 1990 -- following objections from Britain, France, Italy, Portugal and Spain over imports of Japanese vehicles. The figures do not include Japanese vehicles assembled in Europe.
